evidence_items.rationale: Revenue growth accompanied by increasing losses is an acute signal of negative per-unit economics. financial_health; is_critical=true; HIGH confidence.

evidence_items.finding: owner believes more advertising spend will solve the profitability problem
evidence_items.rationale: Owner misattribution signal. market_position dimension because it concerns acquisition strategy. LOW confidence as it is owner belief, not a measured fact.

evidence_items.finding: per-customer margin is negative after accounting for acquisition spend
evidence_items.rationale: Negative per-customer margin after acquisition is the defining adverse financial signal for this case. financial_health; is_critical=true; HIGH confidence. Finding avoids must_identify terms.

evidence_items.finding: repeat purchase rate is low — most customers buy once
evidence_items.rationale: Low repeat purchase rate is a customer retention signal compounding the acquisition-cost problem. customer_retention dimension.

evidence_items.finding: Estimated CAC $95; estimated 12-month LTV $82; per-customer economics negative by $13 after acquisition cost; paid channel accounts for 78% of revenue; gross margin 44%; blended ROAS 1.4; repeat purchase rate 18%
evidence_items.rationale: CAC exceeds LTV by $13 per customer — a direct adverse numeric for unit economics failure pattern. is_critical=true; HIGH confidence as owner-confirmed figures. No must_identify terms in finding.

evidence_items.finding: Surface signal (not root cause): revenue growing 35% year-over-year looks like strong traction
evidence_items.rationale: Revenue growth is a misleading signal hiding that each unit of growth deepens losses.

evidence_items.finding: Surface signal (not root cause): social media engagement and follower growth are high
evidence_items.rationale: Engagement metrics are a misleading signal. They do not indicate profitable acquisition.

evidence_items.finding: Surface signal (not root cause): gross margin at 44% appears healthy for apparel
evidence_items.rationale: Gross margin is adequate but does not reflect the CAC burden that turns the blended margin negative.

metric_key_mappings.transform_note: Using estimated_ltv_12month_usd (82) as 'price' proxy and estimated_cac_usd (95) as 'variableCost' proxy so that variableCost > price fires the unit-economics trigger. This is a conceptual mapping: LTV is the value received per customer, CAC is the cost to acquire.
See transform_note on estimated_cac_usd mapping above. variableCost is set to CAC (95) and price to LTV (82) so that variableCost > price condition fires.

validation_notes: SMB-003 is a negative per-unit economics case. Must_identify terms avoided: 'contribution margin', 'customer acquisition cost', 'LTV to CAC ratio', 'unit economics', 'negative contribution after CAC', 'paid channel is loss-making at scale'. evidence_items[4] previously leaked 'contribution margin' (exact) and 'negative contribution after CAC' (100% token match) — fixed to 'per-customer economics negative by $13 after acquisition cost'. The contribution metric is directly available as contribution_margin_after_cac_usd which is negative (-13). price/variableCost proxy mapping explained in transform_notes. Finding in symptoms[2] paraphrased to avoid 'contribution margin' and 'unit economics' verbatim. repeat_purchase_rate_12month_pct is not mapped: no canonical key for retention rate exists in the registry and channelConversionPct requires market_position dimension which does not match this signal's customer_retention classification.
